newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal to tap mobile phones in drugs war.
newsitem.headline: Portugal to tap mobile phones in drugs war.

text.p: The Portuguese government on Wednesday ordered mobile phone operators to install technology to permit phone tapping and help police fight increasingly powerful and innovative international drug gangs.
"There is no fight against drug trafficking without tapping mobile phones," Justice Minister Jose Vera Jardim said before a parliamentary debate on crime.
Drug traffickers used mobile phones because they knew authorities could not tap their calls, police said. Portuguese law permits tapping.

Portugal's two mobile phone operators, TMN-Telecommunicacoes Moveis Nacionais and Telecel-Comunicacoes Pessoais, had resisted pressure from police to install the technology to tap calls because of the high cost, security sources said.
Concession contracts agreed between the government and the phone operators did not require the companies to install such technology, company sources said.
Portugal's under-funded police force says it is struggling to keep the pressure on international drug gangs, who run heroin, cocaine and cannabis into Portugal by land and sea.
Some is consumed domestically and the rest exported to Europe, mainly the Netherlands and Spain.
